title: Clean cooking that lasts
who_controls_it: Energy ministries and fuel suppliers; households decide daily use
asset_or_service: Stoves, fuel refills, electricity, appliance service
capital_type: Public subsidy plus blended and carbon finance; consumer finance
who_pays_upfront: Public programmes, enterprises with concessional loans, households in instalments
who_covers_ongoing_costs: Households (refills, power), public subsidy where targeted
who_benefits: Women and children first, then the neighbourhood air
implementation_risk: Fuel stacking; refill affordability; supply gaps in rural areas
evidence_needed: Sustained exclusive use and measured personal exposure, not just connections
what_we_know: Connections rose fast; many households refill too rarely to cook with gas alone
what_needs_proof: Whether these models raise sustained use and lower exposure at scale

title: Cleaner brick kilns
problem: Kiln smoke in rural and peri-urban clusters
who_controls_it: State pollution boards and courts; kiln owners
asset_or_service: Zigzag, vertical shaft or tunnel kilns; trained workers; monitoring
capital_type: Commercial credit with guarantees; capital subsidy; owner equity
who_pays_upfront: Owners, with concessional credit or subsidy
who_benefits: Downwind residents; owners through fuel savings
implementation_risk: Conversion without trained workers; costs passed to workers; uneven enforcement
evidence_needed: Emissions after conversion and what happens to workers' pay, debt and exposure
what_we_know: Cleaner designs cut emissions and pay back in a few years on paper
what_is_proposed: Credit lines, partial guarantees, 25-50% capital subsidies, satellite mapping for enforcement

title: Shared boilers and cleaner industrial heat
problem: Ground-level smoke from small industrial boilers
who_controls_it: Industry departments, pollution boards, cluster associations
asset_or_service: Common boiler utilities, piped steam, fuel switching
capital_type: Commercial project finance with public subsidy
who_benefits: Workers and residents near clusters; firms through lower fuel costs
implementation_risk: Demand risk for the utility; transfer beyond dense clusters
evidence_needed: Independent measurement of emissions and costs
what_we_know: A Surat utility reports large savings (company figures)
what_is_proposed: Replicate common boilers in other clusters
what_needs_proof: Independent evaluation of emissions and economics

title: Emissions trading for large plants
problem: Particulate emissions from large coal-using plants
capital_type: Plants pay for monitors and permits; regulator runs the market
who_benefits: Nearby residents; plants through lower compliance cost
implementation_risk: Monitor tampering; small plants cannot join
evidence_needed: Results in new cities and sectors
what_we_know: A randomised evaluation found 20-30% lower emissions at lower cost
what_needs_proof: Whether results hold outside Surat and with weaker monitoring

title: Cleaner air for children at school
problem: Children's exposure in and around school
asset_or_service: Monitoring, ventilation, purifiers, filter maintenance, curricula
capital_type: Public education budgets; parents and teachers contribute in some surveys; philanthropy for evaluation
who_covers_ongoing_costs: Schools (electricity, filters), which is often unbudgeted
implementation_risk: Purifiers without maintenance; children protecting themselves less outside
evidence_needed: Separate measures of classroom PM2.5, personal exposure, health and learning
what_we_know: Purifiers lower classroom PM2.5; education changed behaviour in a Delhi trial
what_is_proposed: Monitoring around schools, purifier pilots, closure protocols, curricula
what_needs_proof: Health and learning gains from purifiers once behaviour is addressed (gap G3)

title: Health services ready for pollution peaks
problem: Illness during episodes in under-resourced health systems
asset_or_service: Surveillance, trained staff, equipped clinics, advisories
who_benefits: High-risk groups and people far from hospitals
implementation_risk: Advisories without services; under 1% of budgets allocated
what_we_know: Delhi has a graded health response plan
what_is_proposed: Integrate air pollution into health programmes, insurance and training
what_needs_proof: Which health measures reduce harm most per rupee

title: One airshed, many governments
problem: Pollution crossing city, state and national borders
who_controls_it: National and state governments; regional platform
asset_or_service: Harmonised monitoring, aligned plans, regional secretariat and financing window
capital_type: Public budgets and member contributions; donor pooling at first
implementation_risk: Voluntary agreements without resources; slow agreement
what_we_know: About half of PM2.5 comes from outside local boundaries on model estimates
what_is_proposed: Five cooperation functions and a regional financing window
what_needs_proof: How cross-border controls work when jurisdictions and funding differ (gap G17)
